system.name: Westerlund 1
system.description: The most massive and compact young stellar cluster in the Milky Way, 15,000 light-years away in Ara near the Scutum-Centaurus arm. It contains an extraordinary concentration of evolved massive stars — Wolf-Rayet stars, yellow and red hypergiants — and hosts a magnetar, the remnant of a former supernova.

westerlund1.name: Wd1-W4
westerlund1.description: A yellow hypergiant variable star in the Westerlund 1 cluster — one of roughly a dozen yellow and red hypergiants packed into this extraordinary 1-million-solar-mass cluster. The cluster also hosts the magnetar CXO J164710.2-455216, a strongly magnetised neutron star formed in a recent supernova.
westerlund1.funFact: Westerlund 1 is so massive it may have formed 100,000 stars in a single burst less than 5 million years ago — and yet it all fits within a region smaller than 10 light-years across, making it the densest known young star cluster in the Milky Way.
